leftEvidence.title: Adam’s generations end with his death

points.label: Individual and shared mortality
points.left: The genealogy recalls image, male and female, blessing, and the name Adam, then records Seth in Adam’s likeness, other children, nine hundred thirty years, and death.
points.right: Sirach describes a heavy yoke over Adam’s descendants from birth to burial, reaching from rulers to people clothed in burlap.

points.label: Source setting
points.left: Children, generations, and death · core · Genesis 5:1–5
points.right: Adam in wisdom and reflection · later memory · Sirach 40:1–5

payload.posture: Genesis records Adam’s years and death; Sirach describes a common burden over Adam’s descendants.

rightEvidence.title: The sons of Adam share toil and mortality

payload.tension: One source ends one life, while the other broadens toil and mortality across all sons of Adam.
payload.title: Adam’s death and the burden of his descendants
